skill.name: nla-fulfill
skill.description: Submit fulfillment text for an NLA escrow, monitor arbitration, and collect approved tokens through the nla CLI.
skill.summary: Guides NLA escrow fulfillment, arbitration checks, and approved token collection.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: The skill legitimately uses the nla CLI, but several commands perform on-chain writes and rely on wallet private keys. Markdown fence matches are mostly false positives, while transaction execution, secret handling, and shell argument injection remain real risks. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Fulfillment text is interpolated into a shell command.
remediation.suggestion: Use safe argument escaping or an argument-array execution API. Reject fulfillment text that cannot be safely passed through Bash.

remediation.issue: On-chain write commands lack an explicit confirmation step.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before fulfill and collect actions. Show escrow UID, oracle, chain, wallet address, gas estimate, and token movement.

remediation.issue: Private key setup permits command flags and environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend secure wallet storage or interactive secret entry. Remove examples that encourage --private-key or PRIVATE_KEY usage.

remediation.issue: External CLI commands depend on local wallet and network state.
remediation.suggestion: Add preflight checks for CLI version, selected chain, account address, balance, and oracle address before transactions.

content.user_title: Fulfill NLA Escrows and Collect Tokens
content.value_statement: NLA escrow fulfillment requires careful command order, arbitration tracking, and wallet readiness. This skill guides users through status checks, fulfillment submission, approval monitoring, and collection.
actual_capabilities: Checks an escrow UID with nla escrow status to view demand and arbitration state.
Helps draft fulfillment text that directly addresses the escrow demand.
Guides nla escrow fulfill commands with escrow UID, fulfillment text, and oracle address.
Monitors arbitration status until the oracle returns an approved or rejected result.
Guides token collection after approval using escrow and fulfillment identifiers.
limitations: Requires the nla CLI, a funded Ethereum wallet, and access to the target EVM chain.
Cannot guarantee oracle approval or recover tokens from a rejected fulfillment.
Does not verify the legal ownership or fairness of an escrow claim.
Fulfillment text and transaction activity can become permanent public blockchain data.

use_cases.title: Complete a User-Owned Escrow
use_cases.description: Submit a fulfillment, track arbitration, and collect tokens after approval.
use_cases.target_user: Web3 builders managing their own NLA escrows

use_cases.title: Support Escrow Operations
use_cases.description: Check demand details, oracle addresses, and fulfillment status before advising a user.

use_cases.title: Test Arbitration Workflows
use_cases.description: Run a full status, fulfill, arbitrate, and collect cycle on a test network.

prompt_templates.title: Check an Escrow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nla-fulfill to inspect escrow UID <uid>. Summarize the demand, oracle address, existing fulfillments, and arbitration state.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Fulfillment Text
prompt_templates.prompt: Review escrow UID <uid> and help me draft concise fulfillment text that directly satisfies the demand.

prompt_templates.title: Submit and Monitor
prompt_templates.prompt: For escrow UID <uid>, prepare the fulfillment command, ask for confirmation, submit it, and monitor arbitration until a decision appears.

prompt_templates.title: Complete the Full Lifecycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide the full fulfill, arbitration check, and collect workflow for escrow UID <uid>. Confirm wallet, chain, oracle, gas, and token movement before writes.

output_examples.input: Inspect escrow 0xabc and explain what I must provide.
output_examples.output: The response summarizes the demand, oracle address, current arbitration state, and any existing fulfillments in plain language.

output_examples.input: Help me prepare a fulfillment for this demand.
output_examples.output: The response proposes direct fulfillment text, explains why it addresses the demand, and asks for confirmation before submission.

output_examples.input: The oracle approved my fulfillment. What should happen next?
output_examples.output: The response identifies the fulfillment UID, explains the collection step, and confirms wallet and gas details before continuing.

best_practices: Confirm the chain, wallet address, oracle address, escrow UID, and gas cost before any write command.
Keep private keys out of prompts, command flags, logs, and shared terminal history.
Treat fulfillment text as public and permanent before submitting it on-chain.
anti_patterns: Do not paste private keys or seed phrases into the chat or terminal prompt.
Do not submit fulfillment text that has not been reviewed against the escrow demand.
Do not collect tokens until the oracle has recorded an approved arbitration result.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps inspect an NLA escrow, draft fulfillment text, submit fulfillment, monitor arbitration, and collect approved tokens.

faq.question: Does it create new escrows?
faq.answer: No. It only supports fulfilling and collecting from an existing escrow UID.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: You need the nla CLI, a configured wallet, gas funds, and access to the target EVM chain.

faq.question: Can it guarantee approval?
faq.answer: No. The oracle decides whether the fulfillment satisfies the demand.

faq.question: Will fulfillment text be private?
faq.answer: No. The skill states that fulfillment text is permanently recorded on-chain.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
